RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, the July 26, 2006/Sravana 4, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Defence; Home Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Rural Development; Textiles)
Total number of questions —20
Non-implementation of  Trade Unions
Act, 1926
*41. SHRI PRASANTA CHATTER-
JEE: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to refer to
answer to Unstarred Question 1510, given
in the Rajya Sabha on the 16th December,
2004 and state the co-relation between
industrial backwardness and non-
implementation of the Trade Unions Act,
1926?
Increase in intrusion after withdrawal
of troops from Kashmir
†*42. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to the
decision to withdraw troops from sensitive
areas in Kashmir, infiltrations from across
the border have doubled;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether due to the lax policies of
Government, situation in Kashmir is going
out of hand; and
(d) the justification for holding talks
with the leaders of Hurriyat Conference in
Kashmir?
Review of military laws
*43. SHRIMATI S. G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to review military laws;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that in several
cases it has been noted that the punishment
was not commensurate with the offences
committed; and
(d) whether Government have received
any recommendation to review the military
laws?
Special Economic Zones
*44. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) how many SEZs are at present
operational in the country, State-wise;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

14
(b) how many SEZs are in the pipeline
and by when these are expected to become
operational;
(c) what tax advantages are being given
to SEZ units; and
(d) how much tax would have been
collected by Government if these
advantages/concessions/benefits would not
have been given?
Amendments in labour laws
*45. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of LABOUR
AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
amend the Industrial Disputes Act and
other labour laws, in order to facilitate and
encourage foreign investments;
(b) the areas in which amendments are
contemplated;
(c) whether there was any proposal to
replace the whole of the Industrial Disputes
Act;
(d) whether the proposal is still under
consideration; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Social Security Scheme for
workers
*46. SHRI C. PERUMAL : Will the
Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to introduce
a National Minimum Social Security
Scheme for workers in the unorganized
sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Spurt of violence in J&K
*47. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Jammu and Kashmir is
facing a serious situation with Pakistan
renewing arms and money supplies to
terrorist groups in the State, resulting in a
sudden spurt of violence and infiltration
from across the line of control;
(b) whether the National Security
Advisor visited the State and highlighted
major lapses on the part of the security
apparatus, that led to the situation going
out of hand;
(c) if so, whether the Home Secretary,
alongwith top intelligence and security
experts, visited the State, to review the
current ground situation in the Valley; and
(d) if so, to what extent these steps
have helped in controlling the situation?
Disaster Management Authority in
Andhra Pradesh
*48. SHRIMATI N. P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Andhra
Pradesh Government has not yet set up
the State Disaster Management Authority,
in conformity with the Disaster
Management Act, to tackle the major
disasters in the State;
(b) if so, what are the reasons therefor;
and
(c) the details of disasters that took
place in that State since December, 2004?

15
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Export of stones
†*49. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDEL-
WAL: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of different types of
stones exported from different States;
(b) whether it is a fact that huge amount
of foreign exchange is earned annually
through these exports;
(c) if so, the details of the foreign exchange
being earned through such exports; and
(d) the State-wise details of exporting
agencies?
WTO meeting at Geneva
†*50. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a minister
level meeting of different WTO member
countries held recently in Geneva
concluded without arriving at any decision;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
specific issues on which discussions were
held during the above said meeting;
(c) the stand of India on those issues
during discussion; and
(d) the reasons for not arriving at any
decision in that meeting?
Employment Cards under
NREG Act
*51. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the district-wise details of the
number of BPL persons and the number of
Employment Cards issued under the
National Rural Employment Guarantee
Act, since its inception till June 30, 2006,
showing separately the number of persons
becoming eligible to and who received wage
among them, date-wise;
(b) the details of daily wage rate fixed in
respective districts;
(c) the criteria fixed, if any, for
ascertaining bonafide of applicants and
procedure being followed for their
verification;
(d) the procedure being followed for
disbursal of wages to the beneficiaries; and
(e) the funds allocated on account of
wages, and to meet the administrative cost,
district-wise, during the above period?
Foreign exchange earned/spent on
export and import
*52. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the details of foreign exchange
earned/spent on export and import of goods
after  the removal of trade restrictions under
WTO agreement;
(b) the view of Government with regard
to earning of foreign exchange during the
free-trade era; and
(c) the steps taken to prevent dumping
in India by other countries making use of
free trading facility?
Single Tea Auction Platform
*53. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government

16
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
are planning a single Tea Auction Platform,
on the lines of National Stock Exchange;
(b) if so, by when it is likely to start
functioning;
(c) what is the total number of Tea
Auction Centres in India and how many of
those centres have localized E. auction
platforms; and
(d) whether it is also a fact that two
more such centres are coming up at
Dibrugarh and Jorhat; if so, by when they
would start functioning?
BIMSTEC pact on FTA
*54. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
implementation of Bay of Bengal Initiative
for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic
Cooperation (BIMSTEC) pact on Free
Trade Agreement (FTA) hit a roadblock,
following disagreements on contentious
issues like Rules of Origin (ROO), sensitive
list and tariff liberalization schedule; and
(b) if so, in what manner Government
propose to resolve the issue?
Kaman Aman Setu
*55. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Kaman Aman
Setu was launched by engineers of Indian
Army, in the presence of Pakistan Army,
on 11th February, 2006;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the utility of this bridge in improving
Indo-Pak relations; and
(d) the number of persons who have
made use of this bridge, so far?
Illegal farming of opium
†*56. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether, according to an intelligence
report, in order to overcome their funds
crisis the maoists of West Bengal are abetting
farmers of Bankura and West Midnapur
districts to grow opium;
(b) if so, whether Government have
issued any directions to the State
Government to curb illegal farming of
opium;
(c) whether it is also a fact that smuggling
of opium is taking place through Nepal
border; and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to curb the same?
Custodial deaths
*57. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) the details regarding the number of
deaths in police custody which occurred in
different States during the last three years;
(b) the State-wise details regarding
number of those police personnel who were
responsible for these deaths and have been
punished; and
(c) the details of measures taken by
Government to check deaths in police
custody?

17
Manpower shortage in BSF
*58. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Border
Security Force (BSF) is facing a shortage
of manpower and requires more security
men;
(b) if so, Government's response
thereto; and
(c) the details of steps taken or proposed
to be taken by Government for covering
more border areas for security, in the
country?
Amendments in labour laws
concerning woman
*59. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 20th July, 2006 Secretary-General.
Asadha 29, 1928 (Saka)
(a) whether Government are
contemplating to amend the much awaited
labour laws concerning women;
(b) if so, the details thereof and by when
it is expected to be implemented; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Branding of handloom
products
*60. SHRI K. E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
a proposal to brand all handloom products
in the country; and
(b) if so, the details of the proposal?

Defence : 43, 55,
Home Affairs : 42, 47, 48, 56, 57, 58,
Labour and Employment : 41, 45, 46, 59,
Rural Development : 51,
Textiles : 60.
